title: Passing and returning structs
recap: Functions can borrow structs through const references and return newly computed structs by value. This keeps related results together rather than spreading them across unrelated outputs.
Read-only inputs and new result values make composition straightforward. Avoid integer division when turning integer counters into a fractional summary.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement combine(left,right), returning Stats with summed wins and losses without changing inputs, and winRate(stats), returning wins/(wins+losses) as double. Empty stats have rate 0.0. Supplied counts are nonnegative and their sums fit int. Rate is a fraction, not a percentage.
hints: Sum corresponding members into a new Stats.
Guard the empty total before division.
Convert before dividing to preserve fractions.
